content.user_title: Generate Clear Changelogs From Git History
content.value_statement: Release teams need changelogs that users can understand. This skill turns commit history into organized, user-facing release notes.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes git commit history for a selected period or version range.
Groups changes into features, improvements, fixes, security updates, and breaking changes.
Rewrites technical commit messages into clear user-facing language.
Formats release notes with structured sections and concise entries.
Uses a local changelog style guide when the user provides one.
limitations: Requires meaningful commit messages to produce strong release notes.
May need review before publishing customer-facing updates.
Does not verify whether commits fully describe product behavior.
Needs access to the relevant git repository context.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Release Notes
use_cases.description: Turn commits for a product release into clear notes for customers.

use_cases.title: Maintain Project Changelogs
use_cases.description: Create weekly or versioned changelog entries for a software repository.

use_cases.title: Draft Update Announcements
use_cases.description: Convert recent development work into concise updates for email or app stores.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a user-facing changelog from commits since the last release.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a quick release note draft.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Date Range
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate release notes for commits between March 1 and March 15.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when your release window has fixed dates.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Style Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a changelog since v2.4.0 using the guidance in CHANGELOG_STYLE.md.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when your team has a publishing format.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Customer Announcement
prompt_templates.prompt: Group the last month of commits by user impact and draft a concise customer update.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for product newsletters or launch notes.

output_examples.input: Commits from the past week include workspace sharing, faster sync, and image upload fixes.
output_examples.output: New features: Team workspaces help users organize projects and invite collaborators. Improvements: File sync is faster. Fixes: Large image uploads now complete correctly.

output_examples.input: Commits since v2.4.0 include search improvements, timezone fixes, and a new shortcuts panel.
output_examples.output: Highlights: Search now covers file contents. Keyboard shortcuts are easier to discover. Scheduled posts now show the correct timezone.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root for accurate commit context.
Provide a version range or date range for focused output.
Review the generated changelog before publishing it to users.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated notes without checking product accuracy.
Do not rely on vague commit messages for final customer wording.
Do not mix unrelated release periods in one changelog request.

faq.question: Does this skill write the changelog file automatically?
faq.answer: It drafts changelog content. You decide where to save or publish the final text.

faq.question: Can it use my existing changelog style?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the style guide file or describe the required format in your prompt.

faq.question: Does it require a git repository?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed to analyze commit history from a git project.

faq.question: Can it create app store release notes?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for shorter customer-facing notes that match app store update requirements.

faq.question: Will it include every commit?
faq.answer: It can filter internal noise and group related work into readable sections.

faq.question: Is the output ready for customers?
faq.answer: It is a strong draft, but teams should review accuracy, tone, and product names.
